title: John son of Zebedee
aliases: who is john son of zebedee
tell me about john son of zebedee
why is john son of zebedee important
summary: John son of Zebedee is one of the apostolic witnesses to Jesus whose ministry anchors the earliest church.
historical_context: This figure belongs to the first-century world of Galilee, Judea, and the early church, where eyewitness testimony and mission mattered.
ancient_near_east_context: The background includes Jewish discipleship, Roman rule, travel, and the formation of a new covenant community.
literary_context: The Gospels and Acts use John son of Zebedee to show how Jesus formed his witnesses and how the church was planted.
covenantal_significance: John son of Zebedee participates in the move from promise to fulfillment as the gospel goes to the nations.
interpretive_notes: The apostolic role is about witness and commission, not private spiritual status.
The Gospels and Acts often show both calling and ongoing formation.
common_questions: How does this apostle witness to Jesus?
What does apostolic ministry mean in the New Testament?
